memory_candidates.content: This codebase has at least 5 independently-numbered 'Stage N' conventions that collide lexically: (1) skill-orchestrate's old deleted single-task Stage 0-8 / multi-task Stage MT-1..5; (2) the generic agent-template execution-flow Stage 0-8 used by every agents/*.md file; (3) the generic skill-body/shared-preflight-postflight-flow Stage 1-9 used by direct-execution skills; (4) /meta's own interview-stage numbering; (5) individual scripts' own retained internal stage labels (e.g. orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh's still-valid internal 'Stage 3.5'). A grep for 'Stage N' across this codebase will always surface dozens of correct, unrelated hits from categories 2-5 — never blind-replace without reading context and confirming which convention a hit belongs to.

When a SKILL.md section rewrite flattens a stepped structure (e.g. 'Stage MT-3 step 7') into a single coarser call (e.g. 'Move 1' wrapping one script invocation), the old sub-step granularity typically survives only inside the implementing script, not as a new prose anchor. Retargeting citations must rename the section anchor while keeping the descriptive parenthetical naming the mechanism/script, rather than inventing a fictitious new sub-step number at the new grain.
